samples: This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table to the console, with a header line followed by one row for each of -10, 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 degrees Celsius, using right-aligned columns. It also exposes a reusable, pure function that converts a single Celsius value to Fahrenheit, with examples documenting the freezing point, boiling point, and the -40 crossover. It only needs console output (no files, network, or other access), so it is safe and simple to use, though the range and step are fixed in the code rather than configurable.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table to the console, with a header line followed by rows for -10, 0, 10, 20, 30, 40 degrees Celsius, each showing the converted Fahrenheit value in right-aligned columns. It also offers a public, pure conversion function that you can reuse from other modules, and it needs only console access (no files, network, or other effects). The range and step are fixed in the code, so it is a simple demo rather than a configurable tool.

This program prints a small Celsius-to-Fahrenheit table: a header line, then one row for each temperature from -10 to 40 in steps of 10 (so -10, 0, 10, 20, 30, 40), with the values right-aligned in columns. It also exposes a reusable, pure function that converts a single Celsius value to Fahrenheit, with documented examples at freezing, boiling and -40. It needs only console access, so it reads no files, uses no network and has no other side effects.
